description: Unified Search — searches across all knowledge graph data stores (findings, fixes, knowledge, errors, rules, workflows) and presents ranked results. Available as a dedicated tab and as a global Cmd+K command palette overlay.

groups.name: Search Input
groups.description: Users need a search input that accepts queries of 2+ characters and returns cross-entity results ranked by relevance.

assertions.description: Users can enter search queries into a text input with a descriptive placeholder that communicates the cross-entity search capability
Users can submit their search query via a clearly labeled Search button
Users can submit the search by pressing Enter in the input field, providing a keyboard-friendly form submission path

groups.name: Search Results Display
groups.description: Users need search results showing entity type, title, snippet, and relevance score, with color-coded icons distinguishing findings (red), fixes (green), knowledge (blue), errors (orange), rules (purple), and workflows (cyan).

assertions.description: Users can see a header displaying the total number of results found, providing context for the search scope
Each result displays a color-coded entity type badge (finding, fix, knowledge, error, rule, workflow) so users can quickly identify the kind of data each result represents

target.label: Search result items with entity type badges

assertions.description: Each result displays a relevance score percentage so users can assess how closely each result matches their query
Users see a searching indicator while results are being fetched, providing feedback that their query is being processed
Users see an error message when search fails, helping them understand a technical issue occurred
Users see a no-results message when their query does not match any entities, confirming the search executed but found nothing

groups.name: Command Palette Modal
groups.description: A global command palette accessible via Cmd+K/Ctrl+K from any page, providing the same search functionality in a modal overlay that can be dismissed with Escape.

assertions.description: The command palette opens as a modal overlay positioned above all page content, providing a focused search experience without navigating away
The command palette displays an ESC keyboard hint so users know how to dismiss the overlay
When the command palette opens, the search input is automatically focused so users can begin typing immediately

target.label: Auto-focused search input in command palette

assertions.description: Clicking the backdrop area outside the command palette closes it, following standard modal interaction patterns

groups.name: Command Palette Inline Results
groups.description: Command palette shows inline results with entity icons and click-to-navigate behavior.

assertions.description: Before the user types enough characters, a hint message guides them to type at least 2 characters to trigger a search

criteria.textContent: Type at least 2 characters to search

assertions.description: When no results match the query in the command palette, a clear message communicates this to the user
Each command palette result is a clickable button that navigates to the relevant entity view when selected

target.label: Clickable result buttons in command palette

groups.name: Search Interaction
groups.description: Users interact with the search via text input, form submission, and in the command palette via keyboard shortcuts. The search requires minimum 2 characters and the submit button is disabled until met.

assertions.description: The Search button is disabled when the query is less than 2 characters, preventing empty or single-character searches
Pressing Enter in the search input submits the form when the query has 2+ characters
Pressing Cmd+K (Mac) or Ctrl+K (Windows/Linux) toggles the command palette modal overlay open and closed
Pressing Escape closes the command palette and clears the search query
Clicking the backdrop (area outside the modal) closes the command palette
When the command palette opens, the search input receives focus automatically so the user can start typing immediately
Clicking a search result in the command palette closes the modal (navigation to the result's entity is a future enhancement)

groups.name: Search Result Rendering
groups.description: Search results display entity type icons with color coding, titles, snippet previews (2-line clamp), relevance scores as percentages, and a summary header with counts per entity type.

assertions.description: The results header shows the total count (e.g. '12 results') with per-type breakdown badges
assertions.expected: Format '{N} result' or '{N} results' with per-entity-type badges

assertions.description: Each result shows a relevance score as a percentage (e.g. '87%') in monospace font, aligned to the right
Each result has a capitalized entity type badge (finding, fix, knowledge, error, rule, workflow) distinguishing the result's source
assertions.expected: One of: finding, fix, knowledge, error, rule, workflow — capitalized

groups.name: Search Navigation
groups.description: The unified search is accessible both as a dedicated tab (/unified-search) and as a global command palette (Cmd+K) from any page in the application.

assertions.description: The unified search is available as a dedicated tab page accessible via the tab navigation system
The command palette is rendered globally in App.tsx and available from any page via Cmd+K/Ctrl+K without navigating away

metadata.author: Joshua Spinak
preconditions: Any data in the system (findings, fixes, rules, workflows, knowledge, errors) is searchable
Command palette (Cmd+K) requires the Tauri webview to have keyboard focus
backendDependencies: GET /graph/search?q=<query>&limit=20 — searches across 6 tables (task_run_findings, reflection_fixes, task_knowledge, error_events, generation_rules, unified_workflows), returns UnifiedSearchResult[] ranked by relevance
